column1: # Toronto and the GTA: the 2026 tables of its three mosques (research Canada section), each printed for
# its own mosque (ruling R30), split forward in time in the local archive (canada/split-7g/): January to
# June fit, July to December held out. IFT's Asr is Hanafi, IIT's and MAC's Standard.
# IFT's table has faults, left out of its split files and named in their headers (proof.md): it keeps
# standard time for 8-12 March and daylight time for 1-6 November (an hour off), repeats 27 March's Fajr
# on the 28th, and prints Isha 5 min after its neighbours on 28-30 November.
# - ca.ift, ca.iit, ca.mac alone, at their units' points (the mosques).
# - ca.toronto (cautious): the three tables at each mosque's point, where each start is checked against
#   the latest of the three and each end against the earliest; and in the GTA's west (Mississauga,
#   Brampton, Milton at the tables' reach) and east (Oshawa), July to December.
# The monitor's captures of 2 Oct 2026 (fetchers/toronto.py: IFT's year CSV, IIT's month tables, MAC's Mawaqit calendar,
# 1 October - 31 December 2026), read from copies pinned as they were (archive/tables/pinned/ca-toronto/2026-10-02/), each
# at its unit and as ca.toronto's member at the six points above. IFT's capture leaves out its own faults, as its split
# files do: 1-6 November (daylight time kept) and 28-30 November (Isha 5 min after its neighbours). IIT's and MAC's hold
# every day and are read whole at their units; as ca.toronto's members they leave out IFT's fault days too, as the split
# files do (split-7g/<mosque>-2026-q4-capture.txt), since a capped Maghrib follows IFT's table, which those days lack.
# On every day both hold, each capture prints the same minutes as the split files.
